Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d748ae80afe6ed63d1c61a51a69f4fb18280c844` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

```sh

git fetch origin 8efaab6e9a65315efd9b415737c26022805f8993 && git checkout 8efaab6e9a65315efd9b415737c26022805f8993
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed

`Test Core (1/6)` fails in `@objectstack/spec#test:repo` on two repo-wide conformance tests that enumerate platform objects. Both are caused by this diff:
- `api-methods-batch-conformance.test.ts`: `sys_comment_reaction` grants `create` and `delete` without `bulk`. The fix is at the producer: add `'bulk'` and pin the bulk create and delete paths against the same rules.
- `platform-object-names.test.ts`: the `plugin-audit` group of `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE` lacks `sys_comment_reaction`. The fix is one registry row in `packages/spec`, declared on #22566 under triage's cross-domain exception.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9f26b002a1dc1225c27b15b3472ad678dcfe3609`
Local-runs: none

PR #22603 (branch `claude/issue-22566-comment-reaction-record`) for card #22566, read at the head above as the net diff against `origin/main` d748ae80af (the merge base is the base tip, so the three-dot diff is exact): 21 files, +1300 / −63. Rendered 2026-10-10T05:45Z by the contract-review subagent inside the owning seat's session, read-only. Inputs: the card body and all seven comments (triage 6092508551, claim 6092717444, round-0 report 6093527449, the seat's answer 6093553917, claim amendment 6093649317, correction 6093657666, round-1 report 6094184898); the PR body and file list; the diff; the head's check-runs. Nothing was built, run or re-run. Where a claim below is "verified", it is verified by reading the code the claim rests on at this head or at the base tip, named inline.

**Check-runs on the head (latest run per name, read in this act):** 35 names, 30 `success`, 5 `skipped` (Auto Label, Build Docs, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke — the path-filtered and opt-in ones). All seven required contexts are `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Governed Surface Queue Guard. Check Changeset is `success`. The file list touches no governed surface; this record is owed by the claim's `Clause-②: yes`, not by a governed path.

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, each with the verdict on how the PR names it.

1. **A new platform object, `sys_comment_reaction`, enters the data door.** `AuditPlugin.init` registers and provisions it beside `sys_comment`; `apiMethods: get, list, create, delete, bulk`; `userActions: edit false, import false`; `feeds: false`, `activities: false`. Widening. **Right.** The object-level create, read and delete bits come from an application set; the shipped sets grant nothing on it (`default-permission-sets.ts` is unchanged in source, and the new tripwire in `default-permission-sets.test.ts` pins that no shipped set carries a row policy on the object).
2. **Create rule.** The `beforeInsert` handler, now registered on both objects, takes the reaction branch: it refuses a session with no user, stamps `user_id` from the session over whatever the client sent, and refuses a `comment_id` that `resolveReadableParentIds` does not return under the caller's own envelope (`callerContext`, operation-private keys stripped). The evaluator is the comment gate's existing one, so no second readability rule exists. **Right.** The refusal code is the gate's existing `RECORD_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` 403 (an ADR-0112 catalog member), the no-user case included — one condition, one code, no new vocabulary.
3. **Read rule.** One middleware handler on both objects; for reactions a system-context pre-scan of the caller's own `where` (`fields: comment_id`, `READ_SCAN_LIMIT` 2000, fail-closed truncation with a warn), then ONE caller-scoped read of `sys_comment` through `resolveReadableParentIds`, ANDed in as `comment_id $in` the stored values the pre-scan saw. That comment read runs the caller's `sys_comment` grant, the tenant layer, row scope and the thread gate; any exception in it answers the deny-all sentinel. **Right**, and the same shape as `computeThreadVisibilityFilter`. Two things I checked beyond the PR text: (a) an application that grants reaction read without comment read yields zero reactions, not a leak — the comment probe throws, `resolveReadableParentIds` catches to an empty set, the gate emits deny-all; (b) the one new nuance, passing the caller's `orderBy` into the pre-scan, is sound — `fillQueryAstDefaults` has already parsed it into `SortNode[]` on the same object, `assertOrderByIsMaterializable` refuses only formula-field sorts and the object declares none, the REST door refuses dotted sorts before the engine, and the `aggregate` and `count` ASTs carry no `orderBy` at all (`EngineAggregateOptions` has no such key; the aggregate `opCtx.ast` is object, where, groupBy, aggregations, having), so an alias-named sort cannot reach the pre-scan.
4. **Delete rule — no new code; the shipped floor is the whole rule.** `member_default.owner_only_deletes` (`object: '*'`, `created_by == current_user.id`, positions `org_member`) binds because the object declares no `sharingModel` and keeps the injected audit columns; the floor test drives the real `SecurityPlugin` with the shipped sets plus an app grant, by id and by predicate, and through the real `deleteManyData` loop. **Right.** The boundary of that guarantee, as shipped and unchanged here: principals outside the floor's position domain (org admins and owners; `everyone`-only anchors) are governed by the application's delete bit alone — the same as every other object under this floor, and consistent with `sys_comment_moderation` staying `sys_comment`-only (the tripwire holds no reaction alternate).
5. **Update is closed at every external door, and the posture does not rest on the hook alone.** No `beforeUpdate` is registered for reactions; what closes update is `apiMethods` — REST `enforceApiAccess` via `apiAccessDenialFromEnable` on every data route including `/batch` and the per-object bulk routes, and `runtime/action-execution.ts` honours the same declaration for flow data actions — with `owner_only_writes` on `'*'` as the row-level backstop and `userActions.edit: false` as the affordance. Outside REST, the protocol's `updateData` is reached only by the import runner (import is `create ∧ update`-derived, and `userActions.import: false`) and by flow actions. **Right**, and the acceptance note "REST door PATCH NOT MEASURED" is answered by reading that machinery rather than by a run.
6. **`bulk`.** `isApiOperationAllowed` is `bulk ∧ child` and `upsert` is `create ∧ update`, so `createMany`, `deleteMany` and `/batch` create and delete are admitted while `updateMany` and `upsert` stay refused. The engine runs `beforeInsert` per row for both `insert(array)` and `insertMany` (pinned: a batch with one unreadable comment refuses whole with nothing written), and `deleteManyData` deletes per id (pinned: another member's row fails on its own with `PERMISSION_DENIED` and survives). **Right.**
7. **Uniqueness.** `(comment_id, emoji, user_id)` with `unique: 'organization'` (ADR-0120 D1): the driver prepends the NULL-safe organization key part. A duplicate is `DUPLICATE_RECORD` 409 at the engine and `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` 409 through `mapDataError`, no new code. **Right.** I also sized the key, because it is four varchar parts under utf8mb4 and the driver documents the 3072-byte bound as per KEY, not per column: the server refuses such a key with `ER_TOO_LONG_KEY`, `explainUnkeyableTextColumn` recognises that code beside `ER_BLOB_KEY_WITHOUT_LENGTH`, and for a UNIQUE index the driver then carries the constraint on its SHA-256 shadow column — the route `sys_setting`'s four-part org-scoped unique key already takes. Not measured live on this object (Temporal Conformance runs driver-sql's own suite), but it is the platform's existing answer, not a gap this diff opens.
8. **`comment_id` as an id column, not a lookup**, so a comment author's delete is neither refused by `restrict` nor made to cascade under the author's authority over other members' rows; orphaned reactions stay stored and are read by nobody (pinned). **Right.**
9. **`@objectstack/spec`: `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['plugin-audit']` gains the name**, so `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` and `isPlatformProvidedObjectName` widen. Consumers traced at this head: lint's `validate-object-references` rung ③, `validate-nav-access` and `validate-translation-references` (a stack naming the object now resolves instead of being flagged), and `engine.resolvePrimaryDatasource` (the object votes for its datasource once registered, beside the three it is provisioned with). All widening; no accept set narrows. The `api-surface` snapshot records exports, not values, so `check:generated` 15 of 15 current is the expected reading, and TypeScript Type Check is green. **Right.**
10. **plugin-audit's public index is unchanged.** `objects/index.ts` and `COMMENT_REACTION_OBJECT` are not re-exported from `src/index.ts`, so the package's published change is behavioural (a new registered object; two installers now gating two objects), not a new export. That is why the plugin-security test re-declares the floor-relevant shape instead of importing it, with plugin-audit's object test pinning the real declaration — the arrangement `ownership-floor-alternates.test.ts` already uses for `sys_comment`. **Right.**
11. **Generated artefacts.** The four `.objects.generated.ts` and three `.source-hashes.generated.ts` bundles and `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json` (84 registered, 49 in reach, tenant field `organization_id`) are generator output; `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage` and `check:platform-object-tenancy-census` ride inside the green Lint & Repo Gates. **Right.**
12. **Untouched, as the card and claim require:** `sys_comment.reactions` and its bundles, the author-only update floor on `sys_comment`, every `content/docs` page, every objectui file. Confirmed on the file list and the diff.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/22566-comment-reaction-record.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-audit: minor`, `@objectstack/spec: minor`. **Matches what the diff publishes.** plugin-audit ships a new object, two gates and its bundles (`files: dist`); spec ships one registry row that widens three lint acceptances. Nothing is removed or renamed, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 disposition is owed; Check Changeset is green on the head.
- `@objectstack/plugin-security` is correctly absent: its two changed files are tests, and the package publishes `dist` only. `scripts/`, `.changeset/` and `plugin-audit/scripts/i18n-extract.config.ts` publish nothing.
- **Clause-②:** `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the changeset body; `Clause-②: yes` on PR body line 2. The arm is right: the diff widens what the data door, the batch doors and the lint registry accept and narrows nothing; `yes` takes at least `minor`, and both entries are `minor`.
- The body carries the two sentences an upgrading agent needs: the B posture ("Granting it … the `everyone`-bound baseline grants nothing on it") and that `sys_comment.reactions` is unchanged in this release.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev flag and every `open_questions` entry, answered or escalated:

- **Round-0 `open_questions` (where the object's bits come from).** Answered in-seat as **B** (6093553917) and corrected (6093657666): A is not barred by the `member_default` ruling but is a baseline widening no seat adds on its own; C would reverse ADR-0090 D5 and needs an ADR; B is the no-widening default and is what the diff ships. Consistent with the diff (no shipped grant; the tripwire; the floor pinned under an app grant). The seat recorded the answer as **open to the maintainer's veto** in its round report, so the escalation is on file; a veto for A is two `member_default` lines plus pins as a follow-up, and nothing here forecloses it. Round-1 `open_questions` is empty.
- **Round-0 deviations.** (1) `Part of` to `Fixes #22566`: PR line 1 now reads `Fixes #22566`, and the check-runs "Part-of PR must not also close its card" and "The card this PR closes must claim this branch" are both `success`. Answered. (2) `default-permission-sets.ts` unchanged in source: the measured consequence of B. Answered. (3) one handler per seam in `comment-access-hooks.ts`: read in the diff; the comment branch keeps its behaviour, the comment suites sit inside the green Test Core, and `check:system-context-census` is green. Answered. (4) two existing plugin-audit tests updated: in the diff, within the claim's test surface. Answered. (5) `origin/main` merged: the head is a merge of d748ae80af, the current base tip. Answered. (6) the card's ablation mapped to A1 and A4: explained — A1 reddens the "cannot delete another member's reaction" pin, A4 reddens the first pin. Answered. (7) translated-locale leaves carry the generator's source fills: the claim said "regenerated, never by hand", the source-hash files record the provenance, `check:i18n` is green; a hand translation is an i18n follow-up, not this card. Answered.
- **Round-1 deviations.** The worktree was recreated; `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needed four unrelated packages built and was then re-run green; the spec repo project ran at an earlier branch commit with the two target files re-run at the changeset commit and `check:generated` at the head — all superseded by the head's own check-runs, which are the gate verdicts here; bulk is pinned at the engine calls and through `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` rather than at the REST 405 — answered in ①.5 and ①.6 by reading the `apiMethods` machinery.
- **`out_of_scope_findings` (three, noted and not filed).** Judged against Prime Directive 10: the stale "wildcard CRUD" sentence in `comment-access-hooks.ts`'s header and the `system-context.mdx` row that does not yet name reactions are prose, not a defect, a contract violation or an authoring trap, so Acceptance notes is the right carrier; `sys_audit_log` recording reaction writes is the ledger's always-on design (`activities: false` stops only the `sys_activity` mirror), with `SKIP_OBJECTS` named as the knob and `audit-writers.ts` held by PR #22526 — a note, not a defect.
- **The card's measurements.** Read rule: measured, the comment gate reused (①.3). Uniqueness: measured (①.7). Consumer census: objectstack has no runtime reader; objectui's `RecordDetailView.tsx` is the one reader and writer at `main` and at the pin; **cloud NOT MEASURED** (no access from the session) — escalated plainly, and harmless to this additive diff since nothing is retired. The pinned console's write to `sys_comment.reactions` is untouched, so no window opens where a member's click fails worse than today; that ordering belongs to #22573.
- **Triage's five pins** are all pinned: own-reaction create and delete on another member's comment; two concurrent rows; another member cannot delete; readable exactly when the comment is; the ablation, with the dev's mapping stated.
- **Acceptance-note "REST door PATCH NOT MEASURED":** answered by reading (①.5).

One observation, not a FAIL reason and not pinned either way: whether a reactor can still delete their own reaction by id once its comment is gone or no longer readable to them is not pinned; the orphan is read by nobody (pinned), and no ruling asks for a retraction path. If a chatter card needs one, it is a question for that card.
